claims.text: Ti-6Al-4V is a standard structural titanium alloy with moderate surface hardness and wear performance.
Laser cladding can deposit a TiAl/TiC composite coating on a Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) surface.
The TiC particles in the proposed coating will be fine and uniformly dispersed.
A laser-cladded TiAl/TiC coating will improve both surface hardness and wear resistance relative to untreated titanium alloy.
The beneficial effect will hold during room-temperature and moderately elevated-temperature sliding wear.
The effect will hold in reciprocating ball-on-disk testing at a 10 N load and an approximately 4.5 mm one-way sliding distance.
Rapid solidification during laser cladding will produce a refined, multiphase surface microstructure consisting of TiC particles embedded in a TiAl intermetallic matrix.
The laser-cladded coating will have smaller grains and effective TiC particle dispersion.
The refined microstructure and dispersed particles will impede dislocation motion and reduce plastic deformation.
TiC particles will pin dislocations and reinforce the TiAl matrix, thereby increasing surface hardness.
A fine-grained, multiphase structure will improve load-carrying ability during wear.
Improved load-carrying ability will reduce material removal and abrasion against a counter-body.
The coating will increase surface hardness by approximately 30–60% relative to the untreated alloy.
The coating will reduce wear rate relative to the untreated alloy.
Improvement depends on the coating having low porosity, strong adhesion, and uniformly dispersed TiC.
Very high temperatures or cyclic thermal stresses may alter the coating microstructure or degrade the coating and negate the improvements.
